source.title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space of dimension at least 3, and write S_X for its unit sphere. Is X necessarily a Hilbert space if every closed homogeneous hyperplane H in X admits a unit vector x in S_X such that x is isosceles-orthogonal to all unit vectors of H, meaning x ⊥_I y for every y in H ∩ S_X, where isosceles orthogonality is the relation ∥x - y∥ = ∥x + y∥?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6.22 Let X be a Banach space, dim X ≥ 3, such that for any closed and homogeneous hyperplane H ⊂ X there exists x ∈ SX such that x ⊥I Hx ∩ SX . Is X necessarily a Hilbert space?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Banach space of dimension at least 3, and write S_X for its unit sphere. Is X necessarily a Hilbert space if every closed homogeneous hyperplane H in X admits a unit vector x in S_X such that x is Pythagorean-minus-orthogonal to all unit vectors of H, meaning x ⊥_{P-} y for every y in H ∩ S_X, where x ⊥_{P-} y means ∥x - y∥^2 = ∥x∥^2 + ∥y∥^2?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7.17 Let X be a Banach space, dim X ≥ 3, such that for any closed and homogeneous hyperplane H ⊂ X there exists x ∈ SX such that x ⊥P− Hx ∩ SX . Is X necessarily a Hilbert space?

accepted.question_text: For a two-dimensional real normed space X with unit sphere S_X, Theorem 4.8.11 relates equality of the Birkhoff and isosceles Joly curves to implication between Birkhoff and isosceles orthogonality on unit vectors. Do analogous equivalences hold for other orthogonality relations on normed planes, such as the two Pythagorean variants x ⊥_{P-} y and x ⊥_{P+} y?

evidence.quote: Question 4.8.12 Does some analogue of Theorem 4.8.11 hold for other orthogonalities?

accepted.question_text: In a normed plane, let S_B denote the Joly curve built from positively oriented unit pairs u, v with u ⊥_B v, and let S_{P-} and S_{P+} denote the analogous Pythagorean-minus and Pythagorean-plus curves. Known equivalences use the orientation condition u ∧ v > 0: S_B = S_{P-} iff every such positively oriented Birkhoff-orthogonal unit pair also satisfies u ⊥_{P-} v, and similarly for S_{P+}. Can this orientation hypothesis u ∧ v > 0 be removed from those equivalences?

evidence.quote: Question 4.8.13 Can the condition u ∧ v > 0 be removed in the properties (i) and (ii)?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed plane with unit sphere S_X. Let S_B and S_B' be the two Birkhoff Joly curves corresponding to the two orientations of unit Birkhoff-orthogonal pairs, and let S_{P-} and S_{P+} be the corresponding Pythagorean-minus and Pythagorean-plus curves. If one Birkhoff curve, S_B or S_B', equals one Pythagorean curve, S_{P-} or S_{P+}, must S_X be an ellipse, equivalently must X be an inner product space?
accepted.context_brief: One Birkhoff curve equals one Pythagorean curve

evidence.quote: Question 4.8.14 If SK = SL with K ∈ {B, B′} and L ∈ {P−, P+}, is SX an ellipse?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed space, and restrict attention to unit vectors in S_X. Choose two distinct orthogonality relations K and L from the three relations isosceles orthogonality ⊥_I, Pythagorean-plus orthogonality ⊥_{P+}, and Pythagorean-minus orthogonality ⊥_{P-}. If every unit pair x, y with x ⊥_K y also satisfies x ⊥_L y, does this implication characterize inner product spaces when dim X ≥ 3?
accepted.context_brief: Unit-sphere implications in dimension at least 3

evidence.quote: We do not know what happens if the dimension of the space is greater than or equal to three.

accepted.question_text: For fixed real parameters a and b, with the two-parameter Carlsson relation x ⊥_{a,b} y defined by ∥x - y∥^2 + ∥a x - b y∥^2 = ∥x - b y∥^2 + ∥y - a x∥^2, does symmetry alone force X to be an inner product space? Here symmetry means that x ⊥_{a,b} y implies y ⊥_{a,b} x for all vectors x and y; the known stronger hypothesis was symmetry plus additivity.

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.2 Does symmetry alone imply the same result?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary Carlsson orthogonality on a normed space X, defined by finite real coefficients a_i, b_i, c_i through an equation of the form sum_i a_i ∥b_i x + c_i y∥^2 = 0 under Carlsson's coefficient conditions, is uniqueness of that orthogonality equivalent to strict convexity of X?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.4 Is the uniqueness of any Carlsson orthogonality equivalent to strict convexity?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed space of dimension at least 3. Area orthogonality x ⊥_A y means that either x or y is zero, or the normalized directions ±x/∥x∥ and ±y/∥y∥ cut the unit ball of the plane spanned by x and y into four quadrants of equal area. If area orthogonality is additive in X, what structural conclusion follows? In particular, does additivity force X to be an inner product space, or can a non-inner-product space of dimension at least 3 have additive area orthogonality?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.31 What happens when area orthogonality is additive in a space whose dimension is at least three?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a normed space of dimension at least 3. Height orthogonality x ⊥_H y is the relation in which either x = 0 or y = 0, or ∥x - y∥ equals ∥(∥y∥/∥x∥)x + (∥x∥/∥y∥)y∥. What can be concluded if height orthogonality is homogeneous in X, meaning x ⊥_H y implies x ⊥_H λy for every scalar λ? Does this force an inner product norm, the π/2-property on all two-dimensional subspaces, or another classification?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.37 What happens if dim X ≥ 3, and height orthogonality is homogeneous?
